_comment: Support resources outside the US. Christine, 2026-11-12.
A SMALL SET, DATED, AND NOT PRETENDING TO BE A DIRECTORY.
Every row below was read off the organisation's OWN page on the date in
`verified_at`, and `source_url` is the page that was opened. Nothing here came from
memory, an aggregator, a news article, or another model.
WHY THE SET IS SMALL. A verification pass over six countries on 2026-11-12 found
seven problems in one sitting -- two dead government pages, one organisation's site
down, one organisation contradicting itself about its own phone number, a country
with no national line at all, an advocacy office that looks exactly like a helpline,
and a page stating two different sets of opening hours. See
docs/safety_resources_decision.md. A comprehensive directory is a promise to stay
accurate forever, and this project cannot keep it. So KRYteria keeps a handful it
can actually stand behind, SHOWS THE DATE IT CHECKED, and says plainly that numbers
change.
DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, and each exclusion is the rule working:
- 13YARN (AU): its own page prints 13 92 76 in body text and 13 92 176 in its
logo. Not publishable until the organisation confirms which is right.
- Rape Crisis England & Wales: its site returned HTTP 525. We did not read it, so
we do not list it.
- Australia's 000 and the UK's Silent Solution: the official pages timed out and
404'd respectively. The app tells people to use their local emergency number
instead, which they already know better than we do.
- WAVE: an umbrella network of ~190 NGOs, not a crisis line. Its numbers are an
office open Monday to Thursday.
RE-VERIFY BEFORE THE DEMO AND BEFORE SUBMISSION, and update `verified_at` when you
do. A stale date is still honest; a fresh date on an unchecked row is not.
NOTE ON data/resources_us.json: it has NOT been verified this way. It was entered
from the charter text on 2026-11-07 and is still outstanding.

resources.name: 112 — the single European emergency number
resources.note: The European Commission states 112 is "available everywhere in the EU, free of charge", is "also used in some countries outside the EU - such as Switzerland and South Africa", and is "available worldwide on GSM mobile networks". It works alongside national emergency numbers rather than replacing them — if you know your local emergency number, use that.

resources.name: National Domestic Abuse Helpline (Refuge)
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
resources.note: Free and confidential. The service describes itself as being for women and children; its page does not state whether it supports other callers. Webchat and a BSL service are also offered, on shorter hours. Corroborated on GOV.UK at https://www.gov.uk/report-domestic-abuse

resources.name: Women's Aid National Freephone Helpline
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
resources.note: Free. Instant-message support is also offered mornings and evenings, seven days a week; exact hours are not stated on the page.

resources.name: Dublin Rape Crisis Centre — National 24-Hour Helpline
resources.note: National despite the name. Webchat is also offered on limited hours; check the site for its live status.

resources.name: 1800RESPECT
resources.hours: Free, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
resources.note: The national domestic, family and sexual violence counselling service. Online chat and video call are also offered; chat was showing as temporarily unavailable when checked. Interpreter service 13 14 50; National Relay Service 1800 555 677.

resources.name: Are You OK — family violence helpline
resources.note: Free. For people worried about safety in a relationship and for people worried about someone else. Live chat is also offered, 24/7.

resources.name: Safe to talk — Sexual Harm Helpline
resources.note: Free and confidential. For people who have experienced sexual harm, and for friends and family supporting them. The site states 111 for emergencies in New Zealand.

resources.name: ShelterSafe
resources.note: A clickable map to find the nearest women's shelter, from Women's Shelters Canada. Not a phone line. IMPORTANT: Canada has no single national domestic-violence helpline — the Government of Canada directs people to provincial and territorial services, listed at https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/health-promotion/stop-family-violence/services.html

resources.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
resources.note: A suicide crisis line, NOT a domestic violence service. Listed only for self-harm concerns. ShelterSafe is the domestic-violence entry for Canada.
